title: idle-sampling-fuse-and-tenant-drizzle-mitigation
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: Recent incident (SUP-732) showed repeated small bursts from low-throughput tenants flipped regional fallback circuits because the global circuit sampler was overly aggressive on idle connections. This PR introduces an "idle sampling fuse" and a proportional-drizzle shedder to reduce noisy churn when tenants send sparse requests.

What this does (summary): Adds an idle-sampling filter upstream of the circuit decision path, implements a proportional-shedding policy that gently trims low-rate tenants ("drizzle"), and provides a short-lived KV quarantine for connections that trigger repeated fast-failures so we avoid cascade restores during recovery windows. The defaults are conservative (opt-in via runtime flags) and include telemetry to validate behavior.

Why: The aggressive global sampler caused frequent circuit reopens and subsequent rapid re-evictions during transient regional egress flaps. This triggered SLO thrash for affected tenants and high control-plane churn. The new approach reduces state flips by: 1) sampling only after a short idle window, 2) applying proportional shedding percentages instead of binary denies for low-rate tenants, and 3) quarantining KV rows for a short decay window to avoid repeated KV-preserve replays that amplify load.

Changes: 
- runtime/eviction/idle_sampler.go: new filter that tracks per-tenant idle streaks and exposes probe hooks to the admission controller.
- runtime/shedder/proportional.go: new shedding strategy that maps request-rate buckets -> shed probability using a tiny sigmoid.
- pkg/kv/quarantine.go: lightweight in-memory quarantine with TTL and telemetry counters.
- api/config/v1alpha: added flags to enable/disable the features and per-tenant override knobs.
- observability/telemetry: new metrics (eviction.idle_probe, shed.proportional.pct, kv.quarantine.hits) and dashboards updated.
- deploy/hotfix/2026-02-20.yaml: hot-restart hooks and config toggles for staged rollout.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design + short RFC reviewed by SRE and Runtime (Diego + Priya)
- [x] Unit tests for sampler and shedder (coverage for edge buckets)
- [x] Integration tests in perf-lab simulating drizzle traffic patterns
- [x] Small canary rollout to us-west followed by regional ramp

Testing & Validation: 
All tests in benchmark-lab were executed against a synthetic workload that mimics 70% of requests being high-burst tenants and 30% being low-rate drizzle tenants. The change reduced circuit reopen rate by ~62% and SLO violation spikes by ~48% during an induced egress glitch in the lab. Telemetry tags added to traces allow correlating per-tenant shed decisions with downstream error budgets.

Rollout Plan: 
1) Feature gated off by default. Enable for 10% of traffic in us-west for 4 hours.
2) Observe eviction.idle_probe and shed.proportional.pct for anomalies.
3) Ramp to 50% then 100% regionally if stable.

Rollback: Revert runtime config or set the feature flag to false; quarantine TTL will naturally expire. Hotfix file included for immediate reconfiguration.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative: the proportional shedder uses a max-shed cap per tenant and an enforced minimum pass-through. We avoid black-holing low-rate tenants completely. Telemetry will be monitored closely for 72 hours post-merge.

release_notes: Hotfix: reduce circuit reopen churn by adding idle-sampling fuse and proportional shedding for low-rate tenants. Includes KV quarantine to prevent repeated replays. Rollout gated behind feature flag.
notes_for_oncall: If you observe increased kv.quarantine.hits with corresponding request drops, toggle feature flag off and notify runtime@sre. Quarantine TTL is 45s by default.
